source_row.rationale: Serum lactate is used in sepsis assessment and resuscitation because elevation may accompany tissue hypoperfusion and physiologic stress. It is not specific for sepsis or anaerobic metabolism, and an isolated value cannot confirm or exclude sepsis. Elevated lactate should be trended when indicated and interpreted with the full clinical picture.
source_row.source_detail: Blood lactate/serial lactate recommendations: lactate may reflect impaired perfusion but is nonspecific and must be interpreted in clinical context; 2026 guideline, accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client with suspected sepsis has an elevated serum lactate level. How should the nurse interpret this result?
